title: Resharding with fixed slots: move one slot at a time, then flip the map
caption: Keys map to many fixed slots (say 1024), and slots map to shards. Only whole slots move, and the app never notices.

messages.label: snapshot slot 37 → B
messages.note: Pick a slot on the overloaded shard. Copy its rows to the new shard while A keeps serving reads and writes.

messages.label: stream changes since snapshot
messages.note: Writes that hit slot 37 during the copy are replayed from A's change log until B is only milliseconds behind.

messages.label: pause writes to slot 37
messages.note: A short freeze (milliseconds to a second) on just this slot, so the last changes can drain.

messages.label: slot 37 → B
messages.note: Flip one entry in the map. Routers pick it up and send slot 37 traffic to B.

messages.label: delete slot 37 rows
messages.note: Clean up the old copy later. Repeat slot by slot until the load is even.

scenarios.name: Rebalancer crashes
scenarios.summary: The map flip is the only commit point: if the move dies before it, A still owns the slot, so nothing is lost and the copy restarts.

messages.label: snapshot slot 37 → B
messages.note: Same start: copy slot 37 while A keeps serving.

messages.label: stream changes
messages.note: The rebalancer crashes mid-copy and the stream stops.

messages.label: slot 37 → B
messages.note: The flip never happens: the map still says slot 37 lives on A, so every read and write is still correct.

messages.label: drop partial slot 37
messages.note: On restart, throw away B's half-copy and begin again. Never flip before B has caught up.

scenarios.name: Edge: stale router
scenarios.summary: A router with an old cached map sends slot 37 to A after the flip; A answers 'moved', and the router refreshes and retries on B.

messages.label: write key in slot 37
messages.note: This router cached the map before the flip.

messages.label: MOVED: slot 37 → B
messages.note: A no longer owns the slot and must refuse, never write it locally.

messages.label: refresh map
messages.note: Re-read the map (or apply the redirect directly).

messages.label: write key in slot 37
messages.note: Retry on the new owner. One extra round trip, once per router.

scenarios.name: Alternative: hash % N
scenarios.summary: With shard = hash(key) % N there are no slots to move: going from 3 to 4 shards remaps about 75% of all keys at once.

messages.label: N: 3 → 4
messages.note: Every key's shard is recomputed with the new modulus.

messages.label: move ~3/4 of A
messages.note: Most keys change owner, between old shards too, not only onto the new one.

messages.label: move more
messages.note: Hours of copying, cold caches and doubled load during the move.

messages.label: switch all at once
messages.note: There is no small unit to flip, so cutover is all or nothing. Fixed slots or consistent hashing avoid this.
